what_it_does_well: A production agent loop whose whole design is constraining the model to ONE owned backend. chef-agent/prompts/solutionConstraints.ts emits a <solution_constraints> block that hard-forbids alternatives ('You MUST use Convex for the database, realtime, file storage, functions, scheduling, HTTP handlers') and marks specific files immutable ('convex/http.ts ... Do NOT modify this file because it is locked'). chef-agent/ChatContextManager.ts is a real context budgeter: MAX_RELEVANT_FILES=16, WeakMap size caches per message/part, PREWARM_PATHS, and a reset() for subchat switching. Tool surface is deliberately tiny — tools/{view,edit,npmInstall,deploy,lookupDocs,addEnvironmentVariables,getConvexDeploymentName}.ts — with edit.ts a zod-typed exact-string replace capped at 1024 chars requiring prior view.
fit_reason: Chef IS the scoped-clone thesis already executed: the platform owns the backend, so the prompt deletes generality instead of managing it.
steal_what: The solutionConstraints pattern — a prompt section that names the one permitted stack and enumerates LOCKED files the agent may not touch — mapped onto our block contract; plus ChatContextManager's bounded relevant-file window (16) and the 1024-char exact-match edit tool that requires a prior view (this is the bounded-repair mechanism: small, verifiable, retryable diffs).

what_it_does_well: control-plane/internal/agentprompt/prompt.md is the cleanest statement of the platform/agent contract I found: it tells the in-sandbox agent what the platform already owns and forbids it from fighting ('Public routing, TLS, and preview embedding', 'Snapshots and forks', 'Injecting any provider credentials through a proxy — you never see raw secrets'), pins the one invariant that breaks previews (ALWAYS bind 0.0.0.0, never localhost), and declares guardrails (do not touch /run/agent-auth, no destructive git on main, verify health before finishing). internal/runtime/{tasks.go,protocol.go,client.go} is the host-side task loop, with agentprompt_test.go.
fit_reason: Templated prompt ({{APP_DIR}}, {{PORT}}, {{LOCAL_URL}}{{HEALTH_PATH}}) so the same loop serves every tenant sandbox; task timeout is a schema-level concern, not a prompt hope.
steal_what: The 'what the platform handles for you (do not fight it)' prompt section — the single highest-leverage prompt idea for a scoped clone — plus the self-check loop (agent curls its own health_path before declaring done) and task_timeout as a DB column.

what_it_does_well: packages/doable-ai plus mcp-servers/ and migrations 050_mode_tool_config.sql, 067_api_key_tool_scoping.sql, 053_tracing_tables.sql — the loop's tool surface and per-mode tool availability are DB-configured and per-API-key scoped rather than hardcoded, and runs are traced. 077_ai_messages_attachments.sql shows multimodal turns are modelled.
fit_reason: Right idea (tool scoping as data, traced runs) but the loop itself is less proven than chef's; take the schema, not the runtime.
steal_what: Tool availability as a scoped DB row (mode_tool_config + api_key_tool_scoping) so a tenant/mode cannot invoke a tool it was not granted — the tool-level half of multi-tenancy.

what_it_does_well: A complete self-hosted sandbox control plane in Go, not a wrapper around a rented API. control-plane/internal/ contains cgroup/, egress/, reaper/, wake/, idlock/, loopback/, snapshot/, runtime/, sandboxspec/, manifest/, detect/, preset/ — i.e. resource limits, network egress control, idle reaping, wake-on-request, per-id locking, and loopback .img workspaces. snapshot/take.go acquires a per-id lock for the whole procedure specifically so a snapshot 'cannot race a wake (which would start the container and write to the very loopback we are compressing)' and rejects a running sandbox. Idle policy and web port are schema columns (0011_idle_policy.sql, 0021_sandbox_web_port.sql).
fit_reason: If the platform ever wants off rented E2B/Modal/Daytona economics, this is the reference implementation of the escape hatch — and its concepts (idle reap, wake, snapshot-as-template) are the ones you need even while renting.
steal_what: The idle-reap + wake-on-request lifecycle (the whole preview-cost model), per-sandbox-id locking around snapshot/restore/wake, and sandbox.yaml as the declared manifest (web.command, port, health_path) that a supervisor watches — a health_path contract is what makes 'is the preview up' answerable.

what_it_does_well: E2B's own Next.js control surface for sandbox and API-key management — the rented-runtime counterpart to sandboxd: what the operator console over a rented sandbox fleet looks like when the vendor writes it.
fit_reason: Console/management layer only; it does not implement the runtime, so it is a UI and API-key-model reference, not a runtime source. Capability read from repo metadata and README, not from opening its source in this pass — INFERRED.
steal_what: The sandbox-list/API-key management UI model for the rented-sandbox case.

what_it_does_well: Exposes Docker-container code sandboxes as an MCP server, i.e. the sandbox as an agent-callable tool surface rather than an internal API.
fit_reason: Relevant only because Actionist's surface is MCP-native; capability read from metadata/README, not source — INFERRED.
steal_what: The MCP tool-schema shape for exec-in-sandbox.

lane: 8. version history / rollback / checkpoints / git sync
what_it_does_well: Two complementary mechanisms, both schema-backed. (a) Snapshots-as-templates: migrations/0009_snapshots.sql defines snapshot(id ULID, owner_token, source_sandbox_id, base_image, visibility, format, status, image_path, size_bytes) explicitly 'Scoped to the API tenant (owner_token = auth.Actor.Name), NOT to the untrusted external user_id', with internal/snapshot/{take,restore,prune,snapshotter}.go implementing capture/rollback/GC under a per-id lock. (b) Host-side git sync: 0010_git_remote.sql adds sandbox.git_remote_url and pushes on task finish 'host-side, with a master token from /etc/sandboxed/git/token injected inline. The sandbox never sees the token.'
fit_reason: Checkpoint = filesystem snapshot and durable history = git push, cleanly separated; and the token never enters the sandbox, which is the security property that makes git sync safe in a multi-tenant builder.
steal_what: Host-side git push with the credential injected outside the sandbox (never exposed to generated code or the agent), snapshot rows scoped to the trusted tenant token rather than the untrusted user_id, and reserving visibility/format columns so sharing and compression are later slices with no migration.

lane: 8. version history / rollback / checkpoints / git sync
what_it_does_well: packages/db/migrations/024_git_versioning.sql implements the user-facing half: version_bookmarks(project_id, commit_sha) PK'd on the pair, projects.git_initialized flag, and project_versions.commit_sha added for hybrid lookups with a partial index WHERE commit_sha IS NOT NULL — an explicit incremental migration from a rows-based version table to git-backed history without a big-bang cutover.
fit_reason: Gives the product surface (named/bookmarked versions users can return to) that sandboxd's infra-level snapshots do not.
steal_what: The hybrid version model — keep a project_versions row for product metadata, carry commit_sha as the real content pointer, and gate per-project with git_initialized so migration is per-project and reversible.

lane: 3. codegen constrained by a component registry / design system
what_it_does_well: The only repo in the pool that treats 'can an agent generate correct code against this design system?' as a MEASURED property. internal/vibe-tests/ (128 files) is a real harness: test-sets/default.json holds a prompt battery where each row carries {id, category, prompt, expectedComponents, complexity} and expectedComponents is 'used for evaluation ONLY, never shown to agents'; categories span feature-with-constraint, clone-with-modification, responsive-challenge, theme-customization. It A/B's the same prompts across design-system configs including a plain-HTML control target, deliberately withholding system-specific rules so 'the agent discovers what it needs through the project's own files'. CLAUDE.md documents /vibe-test with a --degradation mode probing turns 0/6/8/10 to measure quality decay across a 10-turn conversation, and scores 'escape hatches' (agent bailing out of the system). Packages: core, themes, charts, richtext, cli, lab, vega. Pushed 2026-08-27.
fit_reason: Directly supplies the artifact VERIFIED-FACTS says is missing — the assembly-builder benchmark that block-contract's REQUIRED `eval` field has to be filled with.
steal_what: The vibe-test harness design wholesale: a prompt battery with hidden expectedComponents as ground truth, a plain-HTML control arm to prove the registry actually helps, escape-hatch rate as the primary failure metric, and the multi-turn degradation probe. This is how a block earns its `eval` proof. Also eslint-plugin-astryx as the mechanical (non-LLM) conformance gate.

lane: 3. codegen constrained by a component registry / design system
what_it_does_well: A format spec for handing a visual identity to a coding agent. PHILOSOPHY.md makes the load-bearing claim explicit: 'The quality of a generated design is determined less by the precision of its values than by how clearly the intent is described' — a DESIGN.md carries both a YAML token block and PROSE, and the prose is primary ('Prose, not Tokens, is the focus of the specification'). Ships packages/cli and an examples/ set.
fit_reason: Solves the input side (how the platform's design system is expressed TO the model); Astryx solves the output side (whether the model complied). They compose.
steal_what: The tokens+prose document shape as the tokens_consumed input to a block — carry design intent as prose next to the token values, not token values alone.

lane: 3. codegen constrained by a component registry / design system
what_it_does_well: Shows the pragmatic wiring: template/components.json pins a shadcn registry config ($schema ui.shadcn.com/schema.json, style new-york, cssVariables true, aliases for @/components/ui, iconLibrary lucide) so every generated app resolves components through one fixed registry, and chef-agent/prompts/components/ carries the matching prompt fragments.
fit_reason: Least glamorous but most immediately copyable: a pinned components.json in the template is the cheapest possible registry constraint.
steal_what: Pinning the registry in the scaffold template itself (components.json + aliases) so constraint is a property of the project, not of the prompt.

what_it_does_well: Demonstrates the ONE-golden-template model rather than a template zoo: template/ is a single complete Vite+TS+Tailwind+shadcn+Convex app (convex/, src/{App,SignInForm,SignOutButton}.tsx, components.json, tailwind.config.js, tsconfig.*), the prompt layer switches it in via SystemPromptOptions.includeTemplate in solutionConstraints.ts, and make-bootstrap-snapshot.js prebuilds it so cold starts skip install. auth is pre-wired in the template (convex/http.ts is declared locked).
fit_reason: For a scoped clone the template hub should start as ONE excellent opinionated scaffold with auth/DB/registry pre-wired, not a library — this is that, in production.
steal_what: One golden template + a prebuilt bootstrap snapshot for cold-start latency + the includeTemplate prompt toggle + declaring specific template files LOCKED so the agent extends rather than rewrites the scaffold.

what_it_does_well: Templates as first-class runtime objects rather than repo folders: internal/preset/ and internal/recipes/ plus migrations 0017_app_runtime_preset.sql define named runtime presets, and 0009_snapshots.sql's snapshots-as-templates lets any sandbox be frozen into a reusable base cloned via 'the existing ProvisionFromTemplate path'. internal/detect/ and internal/manifest/ infer the run contract (sandbox.yaml) for imported projects.
fit_reason: Answers how a template library STAYS cheap: a template is a snapshot, so adding one costs a freeze, not a maintained repo.
steal_what: Snapshot-as-template (any good build becomes a scaffold) and runtime preset as a DB row, so the template hub is data the platform curates rather than code it maintains.

what_it_does_well: Enterprise Next.js SaaS scaffold (teams, SSO/SAML, webhooks, audit) — the highest-quality permissive base for the 'serious app' end of a template hub. Verified live: Apache-2.0, 4,916 stars, pushed 2026-07-20.
fit_reason: Strong scaffold but generic; capability assessed from repo metadata/README in this pass, source not opened — INFERRED. Also heavier than a builder's generated apps should be.
steal_what: The team/invite/SSO feature partition as a checklist for what a 'business app' template must include.

what_it_does_well: The best secret-isolation mechanism found anywhere in the pool: internal/authproxy/proxy.go is a credential-injecting reverse proxy so the agent reaches its model provider 'WITHOUT the credential ever entering the sandbox' — every agent is pointed at the proxy with a DUMMY key, the control-plane-side proxy strips it and injects the real one on the wire (base URL <proxy>/<agent>/<upstream>/…). The doc comment states the threat model it fixes: mounting the raw credential 'exposed it to the untrusted workspace AND let a CLI mutate/erase the shared file on a failed refresh'. Backed by proxy_test.go (14KB). internal/secrets/secrets.go seals config at rest with AES-256-GCM, stdlib crypto only, key from env or an auto-generated 0600 keyfile, 'plaintext is never logged'. internal/egress/nftables.go enforces network egress per sandbox with a fail-closed rule ('if any nft call fails, the sandbox must not be left running with no egress rules attached' -> status='error') and a boot reconciler that repopulates the nftables set from container_ip rows BEFORE the HTTP listener opens. Tenancy boundary is explicit in schema: snapshot.owner_token = auth.Actor.Name, 'NOT ... the untrusted external user_id'.
fit_reason: Ranked 2 only because Doable owns the per-tenant DATA-key story; on runtime secret isolation sandboxd is strictly better and the two should be combined.
steal_what: The auth proxy pattern (agent gets a dummy key, platform injects the real one on the wire) — this single decision removes secret exfiltration from generated code as a threat; plus fail-closed egress and the boot-ordering rule that network rules are reconciled before the API accepts traffic.

what_it_does_well: A multi-tenant SaaS starter carrying a Prisma schema (prisma/schema.prisma, migrations/, services/, seed.ts) — the conventional workspace/member/invite tenancy model in a permissive, readable form. Verified live MIT, 1,382 stars, pushed 2026-05-30.
fit_reason: Standard workspace tenancy only — no secret isolation and no sandbox story; capability read from repo structure and metadata, schema not opened in this pass — INFERRED.
steal_what: The baseline workspace/member/invite/domain relational model as a checklist against Doable's.

what_it_does_well: A disciplined forward-only migration chain (control-plane/migrations/0001..0023) whose files carry the design rationale inline and name their own boundaries — 0009 states 'See migrations/0005 — do NOT create the `migration` bookkeeping table here; the runner (internal/store/migrate.go) owns it', and reserves visibility/format columns so future features need no schema change. 0008_drop_agent_config.sql shows the chain handles reversal honestly rather than editing history. internal/store/ owns migrate + access.
fit_reason: Migration hygiene is the reusable asset here; the store itself is SQLite-shaped, not Postgres, so the schema patterns port but the driver does not.
steal_what: Migration files that state their own invariants and reserve forward columns, with one runner owning the bookkeeping table.

what_it_does_well: The opposite and instructive answer: instead of giving the agent SQL, chef gives it a typed backend and forbids everything else — chef-agent/prompts/convexGuidelines.ts plus solutionConstraints.ts mandate Convex for db/realtime/storage/functions/scheduling/http/search, declare convex/http.ts locked, and route all user HTTP through convex/router.ts. Auth reads go through getAuthUserId(ctx) and are only permitted inside convex/.
fit_reason: Ranked 3 because it presumes Convex, but the PATTERN — never let the model write raw schema/SQL, only typed functions in a locked directory — is the strongest available answer to row-security-by-construction.
steal_what: Row security as a code-organization invariant: the model may only write handlers inside a blessed directory where identity is resolved by a platform helper, never raw queries — so the tenant filter cannot be forgotten.

lane: 7. deploy: hosted publish, wildcard subdomains, DNS/TLS
what_it_does_well: Owns the product/control-plane half of deploy that sandboxd leaves out: packages/db/migrations/018_deployments.sql and 022_custom_domains.sql model deployments and per-project custom domains as first-class rows, and deployment/ + render.yaml + railway.json + app.json show the platform itself is deployable to more than one host.
fit_reason: Custom domains and a deployments table are exactly the rows sandboxd's wildcard preview layer needs above it to become a publish product.
steal_what: The custom_domains + deployments schema as the layer that turns ephemeral previews into durable published sites.

lane: 7. deploy: hosted publish, wildcard subdomains, DNS/TLS
what_it_does_well: Deploy as an agent TOOL rather than a UI button: chef-agent/tools/deploy.ts sits alongside getDeploymentName and addEnvironmentVariables, so pushing and env promotion are steps the loop can take and be scored on — test-kitchen/chefScorer.ts literally scores '1/Deploys', rewarding reaching success in fewer deploys.
fit_reason: No wildcard-DNS/TLS story of its own (the hosting is Convex's), so it cannot win the lane — but it defines env promotion as an agent capability.
steal_what: deploy + addEnvironmentVariables as loop tools, and the 1/numDeploys scoring metric that penalises deploy-until-it-works instead of rewarding it.

lane: 8. version history / rollback / checkpoints / git sync
spdx: NOASSERTION (Apache-2.0 outside src/pro/; src/pro/ is FSL-1.1-ALv2)
what_it_does_well: The most rigorously modelled rollback implementation found: src/version_preview/ is a 16-file state machine (state.ts 10.6KB, transition.ts 26KB, transport.ts 16.9KB) whose domain types enumerate the failure modes naive rollback ignores. CurrentRepositoryAssessment distinguishes 'dirty' from 'blocked' with blocker in {conflicted, detached-head, missing-repository, git-operation, repository-error} and operation in {merge, rebase, cherry-pick, revert, bisect}; RestoreRecovery records preRestoreHead/preRestoreBranch/targetHead and a resumable nextStep chain {preparing, preserve-dirty-tree, checkout-branch, hard-reset, soft-reset, commit} so an interrupted restore can be recovered rather than leaving a wedged repo. state.ts is deliberately dependency-free 'so the model can move between the renderer and the main process unchanged'. Test mass is ~110KB (transition.test.ts 32.5KB, main_actor.test.ts 34.7KB, VersionPreviewProvider.test.tsx 30.9KB). Separately src/backup_manager.ts does checksum-verified settings/DB backups with MAX_BACKUPS=3.
fit_reason: LICENSE CORRECTION (verified this pass): dyad is NOT uniformly unusable. Its LICENSE reads 'All content that resides under the "src/pro/" directory ... is licensed under the license defined in src/pro/LICENSE' (FSL-1.1-ALv2) and 'Content outside ... is available under the Apache 2 license'. src/pro/ DOES exist. src/version_preview/ is outside src/pro/, therefore Apache-2.0 and liftable with attribution. GitHub reports NOASSERTION only because the dual-license file defeats its classifier. Ranked 3 not on quality — it is the best rollback code in the pool — but because it is Electron/local-first, so the state machine ports while the transport does not.
steal_what: The restore state machine verbatim: assess the repo BEFORE offering restore (dirty vs blocked, and which git operation is in flight), record preRestoreHead so restore is itself undoable, and make restore a resumable step chain rather than one atomic call. Adopt only files outside src/pro/ and preserve the Apache-2.0 NOTICE.

what_it_does_well: BAML + FastMCP + Beam lovable clone — the closest public reference to an MCP-native builder loop, which matters because Actionist's surface is MCP. NO LICENSE FILE (verified live: gh api repos/beam-cloud/lovable-clone => license null), so default copyright: architecture may be read, no code may be copied. Also stale — pushed 2025-08-25, a year old.

steal_what: NOTHING may be lifted. Study only: BAML as a typed-prompt schema layer in front of the loop.

It is a personal fork of the Firecrawl open-lovable project, not an independent implementation — go to the upstream instead of this copy.

what_it_does_well: NO POOL REPO implements row security for GENERATED apps over a platform-owned Postgres. Doable's views (075_vigil_sandbox_views.sql) are platform observability (v_sandbox_posture, v_sandbox_oom_7d), not tenant query constraints. No pool repo shows an agent authoring RLS policies safely. chef avoids the problem by never letting the model write schema, which presumes Convex.
evidence: negative result: regex over all 500 repo-pool.jsonl rows (name+desc+tags) for RLS/row-level-security returns no implementation

lane: 7. deploy: hosted publish, wildcard subdomains, DNS/TLS
what_it_does_well: NO POOL REPO automates registrar/DNS record provisioning or domain-ownership verification. sandboxd solves wildcard TLS + routing for *previews*; Doable models custom_domains as rows. The step between 'user types their domain' and 'certificate served' is unimplemented in the pool.
fit_reason: Custom-domain onboarding must be built against a registrar/DNS API directly.
steal_what: Nothing available. Note that per-customer custom domains DO need per-host ACME, so sandboxd's wildcard trick does not extend to them — that is a separate cert path.

what_it_does_well: NO POOL REPO provides a provider-abstracted sandbox layer that swaps E2B / Modal / Daytona / WebContainers behind one interface. The pool holds only consumers and consoles: e2b-dev/dashboard (Apache-2.0, management UI, no runtime), e2b-dev/desktop, Automata-Labs-team/code-sandbox-mcp (MIT but pushed 2025-03-23, stale).
fit_reason: If the platform wants provider independence on rented sandboxes, that adapter is unwritten.
steal_what: Nothing available. sandboxd's sandboxspec/ + manifest/ (sandbox.yaml with web.command/port/health_path) is the closest thing to a provider-neutral run contract and is the right shape to generalise.

what_it_does_well: Lane 6 has no single winner covering both halves. Doable owns per-tenant DATA keys (workspace_keys envelope encryption at rest); sandboxd owns RUNTIME secret isolation (authproxy so credentials never enter the workspace, AES-256-GCM config sealing, fail-closed nftables egress). Adopt BOTH; neither alone is sufficient.
fit_reason: The composition is the recommendation.
steal_what: Doable's workspace_keys schema + sandboxd's authproxy, together.

what_it_does_well: Schema-first TypeScript ORM (V3 rewrote off Prisma onto Kysely) with a declarative access-control policy layer in packages/plugins/policy/. DISQUALIFYING MECHANISM (direct): policy-handler.ts imports SelectQueryNode/WhereNode/AndNode/OperationNodeTransformer from kysely and extends the transformer, i.e. it enforces by rewriting the query AST inside the APPLICATION process, not by emitting Postgres RLS. `gh search code "ROW LEVEL SECURITY" --repo zenstackhq/zenstack` returns [] - zero hits. The lead describing it as 'generating Prisma+RLS' is false for V3.
evidence: gh search code 'ROW LEVEL SECURITY' --repo zenstackhq/zenstack => []
fit_reason: App-layer enforcement is worthless when the generated app IS the untrusted app layer. A generated app can bypass it with raw SQL or a second client. Excellent for trusted-developer products, wrong for agent-authored ones.
steal_what: The zmodel policy DSL as a SHAPE for expressing per-tenant rules declaratively - but the enforcement must be relocated into Postgres RLS, which ZenStack V3 explicitly does not do.

what_it_does_well: Self-hosted Policy Decision Point: context-aware access rules in YAML, managed and deployed via git-ops, evaluated by a service OUTSIDE the application. The relevant feature is PlanResources (the query planner, in internal/svc/cerbos_svc.go and api/public/cerbos/svc/v1/svc.proto) which converts policy+principal into a FILTER EXPRESSION the caller applies to its own query - i.e. row-level filtering derived from central policy.
fit_reason: Right SHAPE (policy authored centrally as a versioned artifact the app does not own; app receives a constraint), wrong LOCATION (the caller must apply the filter honestly, so it has the same trust problem as ZenStack unless the caller is platform code rather than generated code).
steal_what: Policy-as-versioned-git-ops-artifact decoupled from app code, and the PlanResources idea of handing the caller a filter rather than a boolean. Apply it with our platform data-accessor as the caller.

what_it_does_well: Markets itself as 'Postgres re-engineered for multi-tenant apps' with tenant virtualisation, per-tenant branching/backups and secure tenant isolation - conceptually the closest thing to the gap. DISQUALIFYING FACT (direct): the public repo contains NO ENGINE. Root is examples/, www/, and config only; gh api users/niledatabase/repos shows substantive code only in nile-auth (97*) and nile-js (23*). README states 'We are in public preview currently.' Last push 2026-03-04, ~6 months stale at time of check.
fit_reason: It is a hosted product, not a component. Adopting it means moving the platform database to a public-preview vendor, which contradicts the scoped-clone thesis that WE own the database.
steal_what: The tenant-virtualisation concept (tenant as a first-class DB primitive rather than a column convention) as a design reference only. No code is available to lift.

what_it_does_well: On-Demand TLS is the canonical solution to 'user types their domain -> certificate served'. Caddy 'dynamically obtains a new certificate during the first TLS handshake that requires it'; the handshake is held while the cert is obtained, then cached and renewed in background - only the first request per hostname is slow. Docs name our exact case: domains that 'belong to others, e.g. they are customer domains', and note businesses serving 'tens of thousands of sites'. The mandatory abuse control is the `ask` endpoint: Caddy calls an HTTP endpoint you host with the SNI name and only issues on a 200 (docs suggest querying 'the accounts table of your database'). Config surface: `tls` directive in a site block, `on_demand_tls` global option, `on_demand` in the JSON automation policy. Internal rate limit: 10 attempts per ACME account per 10 seconds.
fit_reason: Solves the exact gap the pool could not, at Apache-2.0, and keeps preview wildcards and customer custom domains in ONE server - which the Cloudflare-for-SaaS path does not do below Enterprise (wildcard custom hostnames are Enterprise-only).
steal_what: Deploy it rather than lift code. The only piece we write is the `ask` endpoint backed by our custom_domains table (Doable already models custom domains as rows). Without `ask`, anyone pointing DNS at our IP makes us request certs on their behalf.

what_it_does_well: Cloud-native reverse proxy with ACME cert resolvers and dynamic configuration from provider backends; supports on-demand certificate resolution for dynamically discovered hosts.
evidence: gh api repos/traefik/traefik => stars=64609 spdx=MIT pushed=2026-08-26T13:29:23Z
fit_reason: Capable of the same outcome as Caddy but its per-customer-domain story is less mature than Caddy's documented on_demand_tls + ask-endpoint pattern, which is purpose-documented for customer domains.
steal_what: Nothing preferentially - pick Caddy unless we are already running Traefik as the ingress.

what_it_does_well: Self-hosted PaaS that already implements the end-to-end custom-domain + automatic-TLS flow for user-supplied domains, alongside deploys and previews - a working reference implementation of the whole GAP-2 pipeline rather than just the cert primitive.
evidence: gh api repos/coollabsio/coolify => stars=61093 spdx=Apache-2.0 pushed=2026-08-26T20:07:39Z
fit_reason: Not a library to depend on, but the closest permissive end-to-end example of domain->cert->route wiring; useful to read before building the ask endpoint and domain-verification flow.
steal_what: The domain-ownership verification + routing wiring as a reference. Compare with Dokploy/dokploy (36,893*, Apache-2.0 per LICENSE body despite a NOASSERTION badge).

what_it_does_well: THE FINDING THAT OVERTURNS GAP 3. 'A free and open-source toolkit for running other people's code.' packages/ holds 64 entries: a core (computesdk, provider) plus provider packages incl. e2b, daytona, vercel, cloudflare, codesandbox, beam, docker, railway, northflank, runloop, freestyle, blaxel, sandbox0. What makes it a real abstraction rather than a pile of adapters is the governance in ADD-PROVIDER.md: a provider PR MUST NOT touch core - 'Do not touch packages/computesdk/ and packages/provider/ ... If your provider can't be expressed with the existing defineProvider interface, that's a framework gap: open an issue ...
